newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly higher on Wednesday largely thanks to the continued strong performance of the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 9.3 percent from 7.5 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 3.6 million lots from 6.74 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the continued bull run on the A share markets was the main factor supporting repo rates.
"Non-banking financial institutions including securities houses were the most active traders, borrowing money to trade on the A share markets," one trader said.
One new A share issue on the Shanghai stock exchange scheduled for Thursday was another factor supporting the repo rates, particularly the seven-day contract, traders said.
"Institutions used the seven-day contract today to purchase the new issue," said a second trader.
Traders said they expected the rates to edge up on Thursday, assuming the A markets maintained their current course.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Wednesday with their yields increasing after price losses in the past few trading days, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 118.67 yuan from 118.33 yuan.
But total volume of the seven-contract market was thin, falling to 995,119 lots from 1.4 million, suggesting that further rises in the near term could be difficult, they said.
